clue.text: Artist, extremely reclusive, seldom seen

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard artist

indicators.note: the extremes of the word reclusive are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shy painter who rarely shows his face in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outside letters of 'reclusive', R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom seen is uncommon, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Practise tries again close to line

parts.note: a court rehears a case when it tries it a second time

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of line

explanation.surface: An athlete keeps having another go near the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries' is the legal sense: a judge rehears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse a play or speech is to go through it beforehand for practice.

clue.text: Rebuke for getting within range

indicators.note: the word for gets inside the word for range

parts.note: reach is the range one can stretch to
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A telling-off for wandering into shooting range territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to scold or criticise them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Record an album and leave?

definitions.meaning: a band laying down the songs, or tracks, for a record
an idiom for departing in a hurry

explanation.surface: A band finishes its studio sessions and heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes recording songs and idiomatically means to set off quickly.

clue.text: Pay for some treat on expenses

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Settling the bill for a treat charged to the company expense account.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone for a wrong is to pay for it, making amends; 'for' joins the two.

clue.text: Standard always set on putting area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is set on top of the second

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
the green is the area of a golf course where you putt

explanation.surface: A golf course's usual feature, permanently laid out around the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a song that stays popular for decades, not a level of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a perennially popular song, and such a song is called an evergreen.

clue.text: Fairly well-to-do peers working on Conservative board

indicators.note: in a down clue the shuffled piece sits on top of the rest
working suggests the letters of peers being put to work in a new order

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Wealthy lords busy on a Tory committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectable can mean of decent social standing and moderately prosperous, though not rich.

clue.text: Fishing dispute: a crowd assembled

indicators.note: assembled suggests the letters of a crowd being put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers to protest over fishing rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cod Wars were disputes between Britain and Iceland over North Atlantic fishing rights.
explanation.definitionFit: The name refers to the historic conflicts between Britain and Iceland over fishing grounds.

clue.text: Nun is over, back briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the word is goes upwards, read backwards
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A nun's time is up and she must return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IS into SI; 'briefly' trims STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is addressed as Sister, a member of a religious order of women.

clue.text: Intensive publicity could get one over-excited, no end

indicators.note: no end says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: hyper is informal for over-excited

explanation.surface: A huge media campaign that leaves someone endlessly overwrought.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant promotion, a media blitz to build excitement.

clue.text: Habitually serious type, West Indies cricketer carrying team

indicators.note: carrying says the cricketer's name holds the team inside it

parts.note: Sir Garfield Sobers, the great West Indies all-rounder
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A solemn character: a Caribbean cricketer who has to carry the whole team.
explanation.walkthrough: Garry Sobers was the great West Indies all-rounder of the 1950s to 1970s; 'carrying' means holding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a humourless, sedate person who is always grave.

clue.text: Porter collecting mail for preacher

indicators.note: collecting says the beer gathers the mail inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so a kind of ale
post is mail

explanation.surface: A doorman picking up the letters for a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman but is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were sent out to preach the gospel, so one is a preacher.

clue.text: One able to deal with a service?

definitions.text: One able to deal with a service?

parts.words: One able to deal with a service?
parts.note: the service tree is a kind of tree, so a tree specialist can tend it, not a waiter or mechanic

explanation.surface: Someone who can handle a service, like a mechanic or a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: The service tree (Sorbus) is a real tree, which is what the expert deals with.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist cares for trees, including the service tree, a relative of the rowan.

clue.text: Bomb English knight planted in station

indicators.note: planted in says the two letters go inside the word for station

parts.note: station means rank or grade in life
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: An Englishman with a knighthood plants a bomb in a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' is rank, not a railway stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb.

clue.text: Spy that's centre stage, strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of centre stage are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A spy who ends up in the spotlight, which is odd for a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy is an agent working covertly for a government.

clue.text: One had, changing oil for pal

indicators.note: changing says the letters of oil for pal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tricked into swapping oil for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One had' means someone fooled, as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a prank on 1 April is fooled, or 'had'.

clue.text: Smoked beef I topped with old butter

indicators.note: in a down clue I has the other pieces placed above it

parts.note: past means old, former
a ram is an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A deli order: smoked beef with an old pat of butter on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one who butts, a ram, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked beef, usually brisket.

clue.text: Sticking with that woman during a depression

indicators.note: during puts the woman inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a depression in a surface
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: She remains loyal while going through a low patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherent as an adjective means clinging or attached, a synonym of sticking.

clue.text: Bound to get on diving platform

parts.note: a bound is a spring or leap
to board is to get on a vehicle

explanation.surface: Leaping onto the diving board before a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A springboard is the flexible board from which divers launch themselves.

clue.text: Disaster in Formula One when company goes under

indicators.note: in a down clue the company is placed beneath the rest

parts.note: Formula One is written F1, with the figure 1 read as I
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A motor-racing team's company goes bust: a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes under' looks like going bankrupt but places CO at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure or debacle.

clue.text: Impression made by politician blocking one piece of legislation

indicators.note: blocking says the politician sits in the way, inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an act is a law passed by parliament
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP makes an impression by obstructing a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an impact is to make an impression, an effect on someone.

clue.text: Current examination involving married male is unethical

indicators.note: involving says the two letters are taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A test of a married man's conduct turns up wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immoral breaks moral principles, so it is unprincipled.

clue.text: Secret spilled about opening of 'Phantom' and 'Ghost'?

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
a secret spilled is let out and scattered, so its letters are rearranged
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A secret leaks out about the start of The Phantom and Ghost films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' rearranges SECRET to SPECTRE without P, i.e. SECTRE, placed around P.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is an apparition, a synonym for a phantom or spirit.

clue.text: Power demonstrated by singular crew

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A lone crew shows its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is a source of power, as in steam engines and running out of steam.

clue.text: Perhaps an orrery some called weird

indicators.note: weird says the letters of some called are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: An odd-looking gadget that some people found strange.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system at reduced size, so an example.

clue.text: A head of state entering church in a suit

indicators.note: entering says the pieces go inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of state in a smart suit walks into church.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a lawsuit, a legal case brought before a court.

clue.text: In a vulnerable position abroad regarding a member

parts.note: out means away from home, abroad
on means about, regarding
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Travelling overseas, a club member finds himself exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being exposed and unsupported, like someone on the end of a branch.

clue.text: Perfect sweet to suck?

definitions.meaning: in ... condition means as good as new, flawless
a peppermint, a hard sweet you suck

explanation.surface: An ideal treat to suck on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint describes something in pristine condition and is also a peppermint candy.
